issues.legal_issue: Taking over the management of an undertaking does not automatically suspend every obligation or proceeding involving it; suspension applies only to matters covered by a notification, subject to the notification’s exclusions.
material_facts: The creditor brought a recovery suit on a debt secured by the undertaking’s goods and mortgaged property.
A notification suspended specified obligations but excluded secured liabilities to banks and financial institutions.
The undertaking’s management had been taken over.
issues.conclusion: The secured liability was excluded from the notification, so the suit against the undertaking was not stayed and could proceed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 7(1)(b) and 7(4) of the Sugar Undertakings (Taking over of Management) Act, 1978, suspension follows only where a notification specifies the relevant contracts, rights, obligations or liabilities; takeover alone does not suspend all of them. The notification in this case excluded secured liabilities to banks and financial institutions.

rule.if: recovery_suit and undertaking_management_taken_over and notification_specifies_suspended_matters and secured_bank_debt_excluded

predicates.recovery_suit: A creditor brought a suit to recover a debt.
predicates.undertaking_management_taken_over: The management of an undertaking connected with the debt was taken over.
predicates.notification_specifies_suspended_matters: A notification identified the matters whose operation or enforcement would be suspended.
predicates.secured_bank_debt_excluded: The notification excluded secured debt owed to a bank or financial institution.

issues.definition: When a recovery suit concerns secured bank debt excluded from a notification, the suit may proceed even though management of the undertaking has been taken over.

issues.legal_issue: A suspension affecting a principal debtor does not by itself suspend remedies against guarantors, whose liability is ordinarily co-extensive with the principal debtor’s liability and immediately enforceable.
material_facts: Persons had guaranteed repayment of the debt owed by the undertaking.
The creditor sought recovery from the guarantors as well as the principal debtor.
The governing suspension scheme did not state that remedies against guarantors were suspended.
issues.conclusion: The guarantors’ liability was immediate, and proceedings against them were not stayed pending exhaustion of remedies against the principal debtor.
issues.legal_principle: Section 128 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 provides that, unless the contract provides otherwise, a surety’s liability is co-extensive with that of the principal debtor. A creditor need not first exhaust remedies against the principal debtor. The Court relied on Bank of Bihar Ltd. v. Damodar Prasad & Anr., [1969] 1 S.C.R. 620, and held that the Sugar Undertakings (Taking over of Management) Act, 1978 does not provide for suspension of remedies against guarantors.

rule.if: guarantor_recovery_proceeding and guarantee_covers_debt and principal_debtor_defaulted and notification_does_not_suspend_guarantor_remedies

predicates.guarantor_recovery_proceeding: A creditor brought a recovery proceeding against persons who guaranteed a debtor’s obligation.
predicates.guarantee_covers_debt: The guarantee covers the debt at issue.
predicates.principal_debtor_defaulted: The principal debtor failed to repay the debt.
predicates.notification_does_not_suspend_guarantor_: The applicable notification did not suspend remedies against guarantors.

issues.definition: When a creditor seeks recovery from guarantors for a covered debt after the principal debtor defaults, and the notification does not suspend guarantor remedies, the guarantors remain immediately liable.
